Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testHeader()` tries to create a CSVPrinter with a CSVFormat configured with `.withHeader("C1", "C2", "C3")` and sets `.withQuoteChar(null)`. It then prints two records and asserts that the output includes the header line "C1,C2,C3" followed by the two records. The current bug report states that `CSVFormat#withHeader` is only used by CSVParser and not supported by CSVPrinter, which aligns with the test failure.

Inspection of `CSVFormat.withHeader(String...)` shows it sets the header array on the CSVFormat instance but nothing implies automatic printing of the header by CSVPrinter. Examination of `CSVPrinter` class methods including constructor and `printRecord` reveals no code that handles printing headers automatically. The constructor confirms that while it stores the CSVFormat, it does not print the header at construction, and `printRecord` simply prints the record values followed by a new line without printing any header row.

Therefore, the root cause is that `CSVPrinter` does not support the `.withHeader` functionality: it does not automatically print the header row from the CSVFormat, unlike the CSVParser which uses it to map columns. Hence, the test expecting the header line in CSVPrint output is failing because the header line is never printed.

None of the recent bug reports offer direct solutions but they reinforce that header handling in CSVFormat and related classes has inconsistencies.

Summary: The bug is caused by `CSVPrinter` not implementing support for headers set via `CSVFormat.withHeader()`. The CSVPrinter must explicitly print the header line on construction or on first printRecord call but currently does not do so, causing the test to fail as the header line is missing from output.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
